html:
Alcibiades was an Athenian statesman and general of the Peloponnesian War, famous for his charm, his ambition and for changing sides more than once. He was born about 450 BCE and grew up as a ward of Pericles. He was a close companion of Socrates, and appears in Plato's dialogues.

  • In 415 BCE he argued Athens into the Sicilian Expedition and was one of its three commanders.
  • Accused over the mutilation of the herms and a mockery of the Mysteries, he was called home for trial. He fled to Sparta instead and gave the Spartans advice that hurt Athens badly.
  • He then moved to the Persian governor Tissaphernes, and helped set off the oligarchic coup of 411 BCE.
  • The Athenian fleet at Samos took him back as a commander. He won victories in the Hellespont and returned to Athens in triumph in 407 BCE.

After a defeat at Notium in 406 BCE he lost favour and withdrew to Thrace. He was killed in Phrygia in 404 BCE, probably at the wish of the Spartans and the Thirty Tyrants.
